issues.description: The problem statement/UML defines SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() as a void method (no return value), but the reference solution implements checkOrderReady() returning a boolean. This divergence in the expected method signature can confuse students about whether the method should return a value and what its purpose is, and may lead to inconsistent implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and the implementation consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to indicate checkOrderReady() returns a boolean (and explain the meaning of the boolean), or (B) change the solution to implement checkOrderReady() as void (removing the boolean return) so it matches the UML and description. Ensure the templates, tests, and example usage are updated accordingly.
